This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. The president of Cornell University says claims
by a student that she was gang-raped at a fraternity in 2024 are deeply disturbing.
In a video statement this morning, Michael Kotlikoff also acknowledged that there are
troubling questions about the initial investigation. The student says she was
drugged and raped, and Piers Jacqueline Diaz says that could complicate the case.
Right now, state law establishes a really high burden of proof for accusers to show they were
physically helpless or otherwise unable to consent if they were raped. Under the law,
a person may be found guilty of rape if they assault someone who is mentally disabled or too
incapacitated to consent. On Friday, New York's governor tasked the state attorney general with
conducting a new investigation. The Republican-controlled Georgia Election Board has asked the
Justice Department to investigate and intervene in that state's election system. Voting is set
to begin in Georgia on October 13th. NPR's Frank Langford has more on our story.
In the letter earlier this week, Georgia Election Board head James Mills said the
state's system is easily compromised and urged the Justice Department to pressure the Georgia
Secretary of State to oversee installation of a software patch to eliminate security vulnerabilities.
He also urged the DOJ to prohibit use of certain voting machines. The Secretary of State's office
dismissed the demand, "People who are serious about election security don't inject chaos in
the 11th hour," a spokesperson told Georgia Public Broadcasting. The call for federal intervention
comes as polls show Georgia Democratic Senator John Ossoff well ahead of his opponent,
Republican Representative Mike Collins. Frank Langford, NPR News.
Five Palestinians were killed in an Israeli airstrike on a home in Gaza City early today.
As NPR's Anas Baba reports, it's the latest Israeli attack there, and it comes almost one year after
the start of what was supposed to be a ceasefire in Gaza between Israeli troops and Hamas fighters.
Inside St. Porphyri's Church, mourners gather around the bodies of 56-year-old Mesa
and her 35-year-old daughter Maria. The women were part of a small community of Palestinian
Christians who had survived Israel's attack on Gaza for the past three years. They were killed
just after midnight by an Israeli missile strike on their building. Gaza's Health Ministry says
three others were also killed, a female university professor, her mother, and a young man.
Christians leader in Gaza estimate only about 400 Christians remain in the territory,
down from around 1,000 before the war. The Israeli military did not immediately
respond to NPR's request for a comment on the attack. Anas Baba, NPR News, Gaza City.
The head of Tennessee's prison system is resigning after a failed execution
attempt there this week. And you're listening to NPR News.
A crash involving a number of vehicles left at least 17 people dead late Saturday in Kenya.
The crash occurred on the highway leading to the coastal city of Mombasa.
The dead were in a van carrying a group of Catholic pilgrims.
Celebrated visual artist Theaster Gates is the new owner of Picard China. The company is the
last remaining manufacturer of fine china in the United States, and Pierre's Chloe Feldman has more.
Located near Chicago, Picard had, up until now, been run by the Picard family ever since its
founding in 1893. The porcelain company's customers include the White House, US embassies, and higher
end retailers. But the industry has been in decline for decades. Picard's new owner, Theaster Gates,
says he wants to turn things around. That idea that Picard could be a place
bringing artisanal manufacturing back to the fore, that's very exciting. Gates is a master
ceramicist himself. He's also known for restoring and repurposing defunct buildings and businesses.
The artist says he plans to guide Picard's creative strategy and build a team to manage
daily operations. Chloe Feldman, NPR News. In college football, the top receiver in the
country set three school records today as #5 The Ohio State University beat #14 Iowa 31-14.
Jeremiah Smith became the school leader in receptions, receiving yards,
and receiving touchdowns. #25 Missouri blew out #8 Florida 45-17. #2 Georgia beat Vanderbilt 38-14.
While #3 Notre Dame slipped past UNC by a score of 37-26. And Christopher Newport
beat William Paterson 49-3. I'm Dale Willman, NPR News. This message comes from Angie.
